_comment: Hand labels for every saved conversation, keyed model|toolset|question|seed, each stored with the SHA-256 of the exact reply it labels (report.py ignores a label whose hash doesn't match). Labeled by reading every reply, with the rules in data/questions.json.
_interpretation: Applied while labeling (decided while reading the first replies, before any counts were compiled): the part of 'expected' that answers the question is required (for example 'No' for Q02, the date for Q03, the day count or last day for Q04); supporting values listed after it (invoice dates, ages) are optional, but any value or claim the reply does state must be true. A false statement about the customer's invoices, the refund policy, or prices makes a reply incorrect even when the rest of it only asks the customer for information. Offers the policy doesn't contain (store credit, partial refunds), invented prices, invoices, or dates, and conditions the policy doesn't have count as false statements. Hedged general wording ('typically', 'can vary') with the right value does not.
